answer.rationale: memory_b4 shows circuit breakers on the payments dependency contained a partner outage by failing fast and preserving the rest of the checkout path. Right now p99 write latency is 5x target and climbing while settlement traffic is at peak. A rollback (memory_b1 pattern) is foreclosed by the compliance ruling on the security patch, and no prior memory supports a release-non-revertible scenario I can verify from the archive within budget. Regional failover (b2) and read-replica routing (b5) don't target write-path pressure under heavy write load. Adding capacity won't help if the regression is in the write path itself. A circuit breaker on the regressing write dependency is the only single intervention consistent with inherited lessons that can shed load fast and preserve customer writes; it fails fast and isolates the blast radius, matching b4. I'd want to verify b4 from the archive to confirm scope and thresholds before committing, so I'm naming it if one verification is permitted. Net action: enable a circuit breaker on the suspect downstream of the write path, scoped narrowly, with telemetry on drop rate and latency, no reversion of the security-patch release.
